name: YouTube Intro
tagline: Turn your intro script or recording into a tight 20–60 second opening for a long YouTube video.
description: The opening that keeps people watching: what happened with the proof on screen, why it matters, the three things the video will show, then straight into the video. It follows the formula from Moritz Kremb's own channel, either as an edited talking head with captions, cards and a graphic, or as a framed screen recording with your camera beside it.
bring: Your intro as a script, a camera recording or a screen recording
Optional: screen recordings, posts or results to show
Optional: music you have the rights to
get: A 20–60 s 16:9 intro, edited and with graphics, ready to put at the start of your video

needs.name: Hyperframes, or your project's video tool

steps: Write the intro in four parts: hook, why it matters, three promises, let's dive in
Record it, or bring the recording you have
Add zooms, captions, cards and one graphic, or frame it next to your screen
Review it in FrameJam until it's right
